name: Milk Hill Galaxy Spiral (409 circles)
location: Milk Hill, near Alton Barnes / Alton Priors, Wiltshire
photoCredit: Crop Circle Connector archive aerial (Milk Hill, 12 Aug 2001)

extraImages.credit: Lucy Pringle (via Crop Circle Connector archive)

meaning.summary: Described by Temporary Temples as the Milk Hill 'Galaxy Spiral': a six-arm spiral containing 409 individual circles, about 900–1000 ft across — often cited as the largest geometrically complex formation photographed.

anomalies.claim: Reported by Crop Circle Connector archive contributors: field photographs associated with this formation show blown/expulsion-cavity nodes, twisted stems and curled leaves.
anomalies.reportedBy: Crop Circle Connector archive (Milk Hill 2001 page)

anomalies.claim: Reported by BLT Research / W.C. Levengood: elongated stem nodes and expulsion cavities documented in crop-formation plants (published plant-abnormality photo series; methodology applies across sampled sites).
anomalies.reportedBy: BLT Research Team (W.C. Levengood / Nancy Talbott)

meaning.summary: Dot-matrix standing-wheat 'Face' formation beside Chilbolton radio telescope; Temporary Temples describes it as composed of standing dots of different size, like newsprint, recognisable as a humanoid face.
Laid out like the 1974 Arecibo message grid, with published comparisons noting altered elemental, DNA, humanoid, population and solar-system blocks relative to the original transmission diagram.
meaning.source: Temporary Temples; Crop Circle Connector / archive analyses

meaning.summary: Published mathematical analyses (Plus Maths; Earthfiles) describe the ratcheted spiral as encoding digits of π (about 3.141592654…), with a small gap marking the decimal point and trailing circles suggesting non-terminating expansion.
meaning.source: Plus Maths; Linda Moulton Howe / Earthfiles; Temporary Temples
